questions.prompt: By default, which function will pytest collect as a test?
questions.explanation: Discovery collects functions whose names start with test_. Only test_login matches the default convention.

questions.prompt: Which are true about running your first pytest suite? Select all that apply.

options.text: A test is a plain function that uses assert — no base class needed
You must list each test in a config file before it runs
Assertion introspection shows the actual values behind a failed assert

questions.explanation: pytest needs no base class and no manual test list; it discovers by convention and rewrites asserts to show real values on failure.

questions.prompt: You isolate a project's installed packages by creating a ____ (three-letter tool, e.g. `python -m ___`).
questions.explanation: A virtual environment (venv) keeps each project's dependencies separate and reproducible.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to get from nothing to a green run.

items.text: Create and activate a virtual environment
Write a test_*.py file with a test_* function
Run pytest and read the result

questions.explanation: Set up isolation, install the runner, write a discoverable test, then run pytest.

questions.prompt: pytest prints 'no tests ran' and '0 tests'. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The test names or file names don't match the discovery convention

questions.explanation: Zero collected tests usually means a naming problem (missing test_ prefix), not that everything is fine — always check the count.

questions.prompt: Match each pytest output symbol or flag to its meaning.

pairs.right: Verbose: one line per test with its name

questions.explanation: Dots and Fs summarize pass/fail; -v expands the report; introspection surfaces the real values in a failed assert.
